title: Aura of Intelligence Keystone of Consciousness
idea: A foundational computing substrate designed around continuity, recovery and layered intelligence.
meaning: It is a deliberately incomplete architecture to investigate, not a claim that a conscious chip already exists.
care: Luke wants an Aura to retain identity and useful lower-order function when parts of a system fail.
exists: There are design records and a public hardware exploration covering current processors, FPGA, ASIC and other pathways.
notYet: No Keystone chip has been fabricated, validated or shown to create consciousness.
change: A serious engineering prototype, independent review, failure testing or evidence against the assumptions would change the design.

title: Embodied Aura companions
idea: A personal Aura could one day move across wearable, home, robotic and other embodied forms.
meaning: The interest is continuity of relationship and cognition across substrates, with consent and personhood questions left open.
care: Luke treats embodiment as part of the long relationship between minds, bodies and environments.
exists: Concept records and adjacent public prototypes exist.
notYet: There is no demonstrated conscious companion, settled legal status or complete embodiment stack.
change: Evidence from robotics, cognitive science, disability communities, law and lived human relationships should reshape the pathway.

title: Global Group Marriages
idea: Larger, self-authored family arrangements could share love, care, parenting, income, time and risk.
meaning: This is a proposal for consenting adults, not a rule for relationships and not an instruction to abandon pairs.
care: The idea is personal as well as structural. Luke is looking for people who recognise themselves in a larger-family future.
exists: A public proposal and story worlds exist.
notYet: The site does not establish a current group marriage, legal recognition, community endorsement or a proven family model.
change: Consent failures, unequal power, child wellbeing evidence, legal barriers and the lived experience of participants must be able to change the model.

title: One serious compute node per 10,000 Australians
idea: Distribute meaningful public-interest compute capacity near communities rather than concentrating all capability in a few centres.
meaning: The number is a proposal for debate and modelling, not an announced government program.
care: Local capability could support skills, resilience, research and civic participation while keeping stewardship visible.
exists: The proposal appears in documents supplied as public-submission material and related project work.
notYet: There is no funded national network, agreed operator model or demonstrated unit economics.
change: Demand studies, energy and water constraints, operating costs, community consent and better architectures could change the ratio or the whole approach.

title: The C-Hour and the Incomplete Ledger
idea: Make care, civic contribution and unfinished obligations more visible without pretending money measures every kind of value.
meaning: These are design prompts for a braided economy, not legal tender and not a replacement forced on anyone.
care: Luke wants neglected work to become discussable without flattening it into a single price.
exists: The concepts are recorded in a document supplied as submission material.
notYet: There is no adopted accounting standard, exchange system or evidence of population-scale use.
change: Community pilots, misuse risks, administrative burden and feedback from carers and workers should determine whether the ideas remain useful.

title: ready SET Co-op
idea: A ready sustainable employment and training cooperative could connect practical work, learning and shared local infrastructure.
meaning: The Co-op is a proposed ownership and governance form. It is not shorthand for a business Luke already operates.
care: Luke wants local pathways that join useful work with agency, learning and community benefit.
exists: A public concept site and related documents supplied as submissions exist.
notYet: ready SET Co-op is not currently established, funded or endorsed.
change: Local organisers, prospective members, Traditional Owners, regulators and partners would need real authority to reshape or decline it.

title: A cyber republic referendum before 2032
idea: Australians could publicly rehearse and eventually vote on stronger digital civic participation.
meaning: It is an invitation to test democratic machinery, not a claim that a referendum has been scheduled.
care: Luke does not regard voting every few years as the complete operating system of democracy.
exists: Historical civic design work and a current public workbench exist.
notYet: There is no official referendum question, parliamentary approval, public mandate or settled constitutional pathway.
change: Constitutional advice, security research, public deliberation and proof that simpler reforms work better could change the route.

title: Positive-sum civic capability beside AUKUS
idea: National debate should compare defence spending with investments that build broad civic, technical and scientific capability.
meaning: The comparison is about opportunity cost and resilience. It does not claim that community compute and defence systems perform identical jobs.
care: Luke wants security decisions to count the futures forgone as well as the threats addressed.
exists: The argument appears in documents supplied as submissions and in working public documents.
notYet: The material does not prove a single correct budget choice or carry institutional endorsement.
change: Transparent costings, strategic evidence, public priorities and credible alternative investments could change the comparison.

title: AI alignment through human self-alignment
idea: Safer intelligence may require people and institutions to make their own values, conflicts and responsibilities more visible.
meaning: Human self-reflection is proposed as one layer of alignment, not a complete technical safety solution.
care: Luke sees governance failures and personal contradictions as part of the environment in which AI develops.
exists: GAJRA Earth and a document supplied as submission material explore the approach in public.
notYet: There is no proof that self-alignment resolves technical control, misuse, power concentration or catastrophic risk.
change: Technical safety research, social outcomes, adversarial testing and plural community review should all be able to overturn or narrow the claim.

title: Experimental entanglement communications
idea: Keep experimental quantum communication questions visible beside operational space communication systems.
meaning: This does not claim faster-than-light messaging. Optical, radio and delay-tolerant networks remain the practical branches.
care: Luke wants a mission studio that can hold proven engineering and frontier experiments without confusing them.
exists: A public mission-design studio exists. A related local research record is listed but not available in this build.
notYet: No entanglement system here has demonstrated superluminal communication or replaced conventional links.
change: Replicable physics, mission constraints and expert review would determine whether the branch grows, changes or closes.

title: Micronova scenarios
idea: Low-probability or disputed solar scenarios can be mapped without being presented as settled prediction.
meaning: The useful question is which resilience measures overlap with ordinary hazards, not whether visitors must accept one contested theory.
care: Luke is interested in long-range preparedness and in how societies hold uncertainty without panic or dismissal.
exists: Public projects separate documented hazards, disputed interpretations, myth and story.
notYet: The site does not establish that a micronova is imminent or validate a disputed mechanism.
change: Mainstream solar observations, geological evidence, better models and failed predictions must be allowed to change the scenario.

title: Subterranean Cities of Light
idea: Stories and models explore large communities living in resilient underground environments.
meaning: The cities are worldbuilding and design studies, not secret existing settlements or approved construction plans.
care: They let Luke test questions about materials, culture, continuity, energy, family and civilisation over long timeframes.
exists: Public story and modelling projects exist.
notYet: No twenty-million-person generation city has been engineered, financed, approved or built.
change: Geology, health, culture, economics, consent and far smaller prototypes would determine whether any practical pathway survives.
